newsitem.title: USA: Okla. Bond Advisor Jim Joseph to join Va. firm.
newsitem.headline: Okla. Bond Advisor Jim Joseph to join Va. firm.

text.p: Oklahoma State Bond Advisor James Joseph Wednesday said he will resign to become a partner at Government Finance Group Inc, an Arlington, Va. financial advisory firm.

Joseph, who has served as the state's Bond Advisor since September 1991, plans to formally submit his resignation during Thursday morning's meeting of the Executive and Legislative Bond Oversight Commissions, he said. The exact date of his departure remains to be determined.
"Our legislative session doesn't end till the end of May, and I want to make sure that they have the support for any borrowings that might be considered," Joseph said.
Joseph would like to stay on full time as Oklahoma's Bond Advisor through March and begin the transition to his new firm by serving part-time during April and May.
The new position is "just an opportunity to get back to what I enjoy doing most, and that's financial advisory work," he said.

"In this case, it was...to become a partner with a friend of mine, John Petersen, someone I have worked with in the past, and someone who I have a lot of respect for and trust," he said. "All the things fell into place that I was looking for, and it seemed like the right time. The only thing about it that isn't good timing is that the legislative session is just starting."
Petersen, president of Government Finance Group, could not be reached immediately for comment.

Prior to becoming Oklahoma's bond advisor, Joseph worked for the Government Finance Research Center, one of the operating centers of the Government Finance Officers Association, he said. He served two stints there for total of four years.
Joseph received a bachelors degree in Political Science from Oregon State University in 1975 and a masters degree in Public Administration from Syracuse University in 1976, he said.
